title: Cyber Risk Manager
summary: Cyber risk managers run the second-line view of technology and cyber risk. They set how risks are assessed, lead RCSAs across units, challenge security and IT owners on gaps, track remediation and report the firm's cyber risk to senior management and the risk committee. Most work in banks, insurers, payments firms and global capability centres.
dailyDuties: Set the method and calendar for technology risk assessments
Lead RCSAs and review the ratings analysts propose
Challenge remediation plans and escalate overdue issues
Review major cyber incidents and vendor risks for critical services
Track regulator rules and inspection findings to closure
Present cyber risk and KRIs to senior management and the risk committee

skills.expectation: Own the technology and cyber risk assessment method and its results
Lead RCSA, KRIs and issue management for technology across units or countries
Express top cyber risks as likely loss so leaders can compare them
Keep the firm aligned with RBI, SEBI and CERT-In cyber rules and inspections
Oversee cloud and vendor risk for critical services
Use NIST CSF and ISO 27001 as the control baseline
Report cyber risk to the risk committee in business terms
Lead a small team of risk analysts
Challenge technology and business owners on risk and remediation
Link cyber risk to the firm's risk appetite
Review resilience and recovery testing for critical services
Review major incidents and their lessons
Cover DPDP Act and privacy risks

certifications.why: The certificate most technology risk manager posts ask for.
Often listed with CRISC and CISM.
